proposed_from.topic:
Sharp optimal-personalized-treatment-value estimation with jointly growing treatment menus and sparse categorical patient groups. For every n>=1,d>=1,K>=2, observe n iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], A in [K], Y binary, under consistency and conditional exchangeability. Allow arbitrary unknown masses p_x, unrestricted conditional outcome means mu_ax in [0,1], and unknown propensities with sum_a e_ax=1 and 1/(2K)<=e_ax<=2/K on positive-mass cells; null cells, exact ties and boundary means are legal. Target Vstar=sum_x p_x max_a mu_ax and R(n,d,K)=inf over all estimators sup over this law class of mean squared error. Derive an explicit all-regime rate, including every logarithm, transition and saturation branch, bounded above and below by R with absolute constants independent of n,d,K. Construct a total computable attaining estimator and matching same-class all-estimator converse. Determine necessary and sufficient consistency and parametric-MSE conditions for arbitrary dimension sequences. The exact rate and estimator mechanics are outputs; an unevaluated optimization or fixed-K constants do not solve the kernel. Preserve unknown masses and logging in the upper bound; known-uniform lower subexperiments are legal. Recover d=1 and K=2 benchmarks independently, without replacing the full joint theorem by those slices or the presolved K>=d^2 region. Consumer: the unrestricted attainable-value benchmark for maq/grf multi-arm treatment targeting as intervention menus expand; this does not replace learned-policy inference or claim a full budget-curve result. The legal d=2,K=3 unequal-propensity witness has Vstar=43/50 with switching maximizing arms. Put the dimension-uniform approximation/variance and matching mixture geometry in the headline; do not silently narrow or downgrade if it fails.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A centered random winner in every patient group yields an exact fixed-sample likelihood-mixture identity with a binomial count of coinciding winners. Its derived lower risk is c min{1,dK log(1+sqrt(K/d))/n}; a total empirical cell-weighted maximum has upper risk C min{1,dK log(eK)/n} on the full unknown-mass and unknown-propensity class. These match for K>=d^2. The one-group passive benchmark and a grouped-arm reduction to the binary parent also yield the bounded-d-and-K parametric criterion. Small exact likelihood calculations passed; null cells, ties, boundary means, unequal logging, saturation, adaptive best-mean prior art, and the known-logging Bayes-accuracy reduction were checked. These are unverified derivations, not a solved full frontier.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Open Lemma J must jointly control approximation bias, factorial covariance, and normalized moment-prior separation with absolute constants, closing 2<K<d^2 and the full consistency boundary for arbitrary masses and propensities.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the first certificate on the K=64 Boolean slice at degrees 4,7,8 and compute its exact lifted variance. A verified dual bound or rigorous OR obstruction must support any refutation; floating-point LP output alone cannot. Stop a route that hides K in its constants.

seed_details.one_line: Sharp all-regime minimax MSE for unrestricted optimal-treatment value with jointly growing patient groups and treatment menus.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the sharp all-regime minimax MSE for unrestricted optimal-treatment value when both \(d\) and \(K\) grow.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the binary absolute-value surrogate by a permutation-symmetric approximation of the \(K\)-ary ratio maximum whose factorial lift has dimension-uniform covariance, and match it by legal normalized block priors.
seed_details.referee_objection: The rate is immediate from applying a one-group maximum estimator independently in every patient group.
seed_details.rebuttal: Independent cellwise bounds lose the unknown-mass occupancy geometry and do not match the centered winner lower mixture for \(2<K<d^2\); neither HAVER nor the binary parent supplies the required joint certificate.
seed_details.burned_reason: Chosen all-regime angle discharged only the K>=d^2 region; the proposed salvage repeated the unresolved dimension-uniform certificate without a construction.

seed_details.one_line: Dimension-uniform primal--dual approximation certificate for the multinomially lifted \(K\)-ary maximum.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Establish the approximation-versus-variance and dual-mixture certificate missing between the binary and many-arm boundary regions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a scalar best approximant and independent coordinate variance calculation by a symmetric multivariate approximant with its complete factorial covariance matrix.
seed_details.referee_objection: Polynomial approximation and moment matching already give the certificate by standard duality.
seed_details.rebuttal: Standard duality controls uniform error but not the weighted mixed-moment tail or lifted covariance; Spalek's OR restriction also forces degree growth that the variance calculation must explicitly pay for.
seed_details.status: survived as the load-bearing open lemma

seed_details.one_line: Exact passive Bernoulli maximum-mean minimax MSE for one patient group and arbitrary \(K\).
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Close the global all-estimator converse left open by the instance-dependent HAVER analysis.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn HAVER's tail-integrated upper analysis into a bounded-parameter mixture converse that remains valid at ties and Bernoulli boundaries.
seed_details.referee_objection: The worst-case \(K\log K/N\) rate follows immediately from the empirical maximum.
seed_details.rebuttal: That observation proves only an upper bound; the centered random-winner mixture is needed to show the passive logarithmic price is unavoidable for every estimator.
seed_details.status: survived as a mandatory benchmark, not the chosen paper

seed_details.one_line: Cell-weighted HAVER under random group occupancy and unknown overlap-bounded logging.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine whether head averaging survives multinomial group and treatment counts without known nuisance probabilities.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition jointly on random group and arm counts, then aggregate the head-selection errors with empirical group weights instead of fixed arm totals.
seed_details.referee_objection: Conditioning on the counts reduces the problem exactly to HAVER in each cell.
seed_details.rebuttal: The target also contains unknown group masses, null groups, and dependence among all multinomial counts; conditioning does not control the squared error of the random weighted sum uniformly.
seed_details.status: survived but subsumed by the chosen full frontier

seed_details.one_line: Polynomial-time compressed factorial estimator matching the information-theoretic many-arm frontier.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Remove tensor enumeration and numerical instability from an approximation-theoretic attaining estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Represent the symmetric local polynomial in an orbit or recurrence basis whose evaluation and covariance certificate are polynomial in \(n,d,K\).
seed_details.referee_objection: Low total degree automatically makes factorial-moment estimation computationally efficient.
seed_details.rebuttal: A degree-\(L\) polynomial in \(K\) variables has \(\binom{K+L}{L}\) coefficients, so low degree alone does not prevent exponential dependence on the treatment menu.
seed_details.status: retained as a required property of the chosen estimator, not a separate kernel

seed_details.one_line: Best-versus-runner-up margin phase diagram for the transition to parametric MSE.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Quantify how mass near multiway tie faces changes the many-arm optimal-value minimax rate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace worst-case tie-fan approximation bias by a sum weighted by the distribution of the best-versus-second-best gap, while imposing the same restriction on the lower mixture.
seed_details.referee_objection: Whitehouse et al.'s controlled gap density already gives the parametric transition.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem is an asymptotic upper result conditional on nuisance rates; it does not give a growing-\(d,K\) minimax phase diagram or a matching restricted-class converse.
seed_details.status: survived but deferred because it changes the unrestricted law class

seed_details.one_line: Honest minimax expected-length confidence intervals for optimal value at ties and sparse cells.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Construct dimension-uniform honest intervals and characterize their diameter frontier over the unrestricted class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace asymptotic remainder conditions by an observable approximation-bias envelope or test inversion that remains valid in sparse occupancy regimes.
seed_details.referee_objection: A Wald interval around the smoothed estimator already handles ties.
seed_details.rebuttal: Published Wald results impose asymptotic growth and nuisance conditions and do not control minimax expected length when approximation bias is first-order and cell counts vanish.
seed_details.status: survived but deferred until the point-risk modulus is known

seed_details.one_line: Growing-dimension semiparametric efficiency bound on the unique-winner submodel.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Determine the efficiency loss from \(K\)-dependent overlap when the maximizing arm is unique in every positive-mass group.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Evaluate the canonical-gradient variance uniformly over a triangular array with \(e_{ax}\asymp K^{-1}\) rather than fixed overlap.
seed_details.referee_objection: The influence function is already published and substituting \(e_{ax}\asymp K^{-1}\) is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: A nontrivial version would need an attainable triangular-array bound and a divergence frontier, but the unrestricted target's exact ties make this a strict regular submodel rather than the main problem.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 because the novelty delta collapses on the regular submodel

seed_details.one_line: Non-Gaussian boundary limit law for a smoothed or polynomial optimal-value estimator when the effective tie fan diverges.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Locate the triangular-array boundary where stabilized Gaussian inference gives way to a maximum- or approximation-driven non-Gaussian limit.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain the leading smoothing or polynomial bias and the diverging tie-face empirical process instead of forcing both into an \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) remainder.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is a standard Gaussian-maximum limit after centering.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sparse random denominators and a tunable nonsmooth surrogate couple bias and stochastic terms, so the candidate limit is not the populated Gaussian maximum treated by existing high-dimensional CLTs.
seed_details.status: deferred because the centering and scaling depend on the unresolved minimax envelope

seed_details.one_line: Joint value-estimation and unrestricted-policy regret frontier for expanding treatment menus.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Relate error in estimating oracle attainable value to regret of deploying an unrestricted categorical policy.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple value-functional testing alternatives to policy-selection alternatives rather than analyzing uniform score concentration over a fixed restricted policy class.
seed_details.referee_objection: Zhou et al. already give minimax multi-action policy regret.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their comparator is the best policy in a restricted class and their loss is regret; the unrestricted oracle-value MSE can remain hard even when many maximizing policies have zero regret.
seed_details.status: dropped after Step 1 because it changes the estimand and loss

seed_details.one_line: Permutation-inverted finite-sample interval for optimal value under exchangeable logged treatment labels.
seed_details.anchor_open_problem: Seek exact coverage by treatment-label symmetry rather than an asymptotic Wald approximation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct a null-invariant orbit for the maximized causal value while preserving the observed outcomes and unknown logging law.
seed_details.referee_objection: Unknown unequal propensities destroy treatment-label exchangeability, so the proposed permutation group is not a symmetry of the experiment.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds on the stated law class; searches found no exact symmetry action that preserves both outcomes and arbitrary overlap-comparable logging.
seed_details.status: dropped at Step 0; named M17 search obstruction

proposed_from.literature_map: Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Theorem 1 and Sections 5--7) characterize pathwise differentiability of optimal value and construct online one-step inference at fixed complexity; exact ties remain the source of nonregularity rather than a finite-sample minimax analysis. Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis (2025, Theorem 1 and the conclusion) smooth the same maximum with a softmax orthogonal score and obtain root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity under a gap-density condition and nuisance rates; their paper explicitly leaves data-adaptive smoothing and irregular efficiency open. Nguyen, Barrett, and Jun (2025, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 3) construct HAVER by a lower-confidence pivot and head averaging and prove instance-dependent MSE upper bounds for passively sampled arm means; the theorem has no random patient groups, no causal logging layer, and no global all-estimator converse. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015, Sections I--II and the estimator/lower-bound sections) split smooth from nonsmooth cells, estimate polynomial surrogates by factorial moments, and pair the construction with fuzzy hypotheses; their proved rates cover additive univariate probability functionals, not a multivariate ratio maximum. Wu and Yang (2016, Theorem 1 and Sections IV--V) make approximation--moment duality determine both the entropy estimator and its lower mixture, including the consistency threshold; the destination here first changes at the multivariate polynomial and multinomial covariance step. Cai and Low (2011, Theorems 1 and 5) provide the closest normal-means template for a kinked functional, but their coordinatewise absolute-value geometry does not control a growing simplex of tie faces. Spalek (2008, Theorem 7) gives an explicit dual polynomial proving the square-root approximate-degree obstruction for Boolean OR; the Boolean restriction of the many-arm maximum therefore rules out any dimension-free low-degree certificate, although approximate degree alone is not a statistical lower bound. Luedtke and van der Laan (2018, Theorems 1--2) treat maxima with growing index sets by stabilized one-step methods and asymptotic coverage under growth and remainder conditions, not sparse multinomial cells. Zhou, Athey, and Wager (2023, Theorem 2) obtain policy-regret bounds over restricted policy classes; their decision loss is distinct from MSE for the unrestricted oracle value. The searches for discrete multiclass Bayes-accuracy estimation, grouped maximum-mean minimax risk, and polynomial estimation of a sum of conditional maxima found classification-error estimation and generic functional-estimation papers, but no result occupying the exact unknown-mass, unknown-logging, jointly growing \(d,K\) target--method pair.
